transcript:
User: Hello — I got your flyer about after-hours calls. We miss calls when we're out on jobs.
Agent: Got it, thanks for calling that out — a lot of folks who call from that flyer say the same thing. When a call comes in and you’re out on a job, what usually happens to that caller — does it just ring out, go to voicemail, or something else?
User: It usually goes to voicemail when we're out on a job.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense — and most people don’t love leaving voicemails anymore. Do those callers usually leave a message for you, or do you think a lot of them just hang up and move on to the next company?
User: About 8 missed calls a week go to voicemail. Many just hang up and move on.
Agent: Yeah, that adds up fast — 8 a week is a lot of people slipping away. When those calls come in after hours or when you’re tied up on a job, what would you *want* to happen instead of them hitting voicemail?
User: I'd want someone to answer and book appointments for us.
Agent: Totally hear you — that’s exactly the gap we focus on. Has anyone ever actually walked you through what those 8 missed calls a week are costing you in lost appointments?
User: No, nobody has done that yet.
Agent: Gotcha, thanks for being straight with me. Mind if we do a quick back-of-the-napkin calculation together—takes like 30 seconds—so you can see what those 8 missed calls a week might really be costing?
User: Sure, let's do the calculation. I'm curious to see what those missed calls might be costing us.
Agent: Nice, love it. So ballpark for you — out of those calls that hit voicemail, what percentage do you think would actually book a job if someone picked up… maybe half, 60%, what feels right?
User: About 50% would book if someone answered.
Agent: Got it, 50% makes sense. And roughly what’s your average job worth for one of those calls — are we talking more like $300, $500, $800?
User: Our average job value is about $2,500.
Agent: So with your numbers, you’re looking at roughly $4,300 a month walking away just from those missed calls. So… with that in mind, would you be open to a quick 20‑minute walkthrough this week where we show you exactly how we can turn those missed calls into booked $2,500 jobs for you?
User: Yes, I'd be open to a 20-minute walkthrough this week to see how you can help us.
Agent: Awesome, that sounds good. So I can get that walkthrough set up for you, what’s your first name?
User: It's Susan. Looking forward to seeing how this service can help us.
Agent: Nice to meet you, Susan. And what’s your last name, so I make sure Jay has you down correctly?
User: My last name is Park. Please make sure everything is correct for the live call.
Agent: Thanks, Susan Park, got it. What’s the name of your company so I can have that on the calendar for Jay?
User: The name of my company is Cornerstone Remodeling.
Agent: Perfect, Cornerstone Remodeling, got it. And just to confirm, is the number you’re calling from now the best number for your text confirmation and for Jay to reach you?
User: The best contact number is +13039150001 for text confirmation and the live call.
Agent: Perfect, thanks for confirming, Susan. One moment while I check availability — would you prefer later today or tomorrow for that 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay?
Agent: Got it, thanks. Since we’re looking at this week, which day works better for you for that 20‑minute call with Jay — later today, tomorrow, or another specific day?
User: Tomorrow would be better for the walkthrough.
Agent: Nice, tomorrow works. I can get you in at 10:30 or 11:15 tomorrow morning Mountain time — which one’s better for your schedule?
User: 10:30 Mountain time works for me. Please book it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that 10:30 Mountain time slot for you.
Agent: Thanks, Susan! Your 10:30am Mountain time walkthrough with Jay tomorrow is all set. You’ll get a text in a moment with the confirmation — you can tap to add it to your calendar or reschedule if anything changes. Is there anything else I can help you with right now?
